■ SUMMARY
We have developed a ligand-free Ni(0)-catalyzed [2 + 2 + 2]
cycloaddition of 1,5-bisallenes with mono- and disubstituted
alkynes, afording 6,6-fused bicyclic hexahydroisoquinolines
with excellent chemo- and regioselectivity under mild
conditions. Notably, head-to-tail bisallene cyclization predom-
inates, and high regioselectivity is observed for monosub
stituted alkynes. Furthermore, DFT studies suggest that the
observed head-to-tail selectivity arises from two competing
pathways, both initiated by oxidative cyclization between the
allene and the alkyne. Finally, the geometry of the metal-
lacyclopentene intermediate plays a key role in directing the
reactivity and selectivity, underscoring the importance of
catalyst design in future eforts to control the regioselectivity in
these transformations.
